newsitem.title: UK: Pendragon says makes good start to 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pendragon says makes good start to 1997.

text.p: Britain's Pendragon Plc said on Monday it had made a good start to 1997 and that the UK new car market remains "fairly buoyant".
"Our trading performance in 1997 has started well, with increases in contribution from our core businesses," chairman Sir Nigel Rudd told the annual general meeting.
Pendragon sells new and used vehicles and also deals in hire and post-sale service for cars in the UK.

"Increased sales of specialist and luxury cars, together with higher activity levels in our contract hire division, have improved the overall profitability of Pendragon in the first quarter," Rudd said.

He said UK registrations increased by 3.5 percent in the first quarter and while demand for new cars from individuals remained weak, the fleet sector, specialist and niche models, and luxury brands continued to increase market share.
